Key points: script scripts/resend_failed_sms.py, run it once. Use queue_sms with original template_id and params. R12 mentions deduplication ambiguity: "If a household appears in multiple failed messages, one new text per failed message would be queued unless deduplicated per household." Done-when: "every household whose text failed gets exactly one new text with the same message". So dedupe per household — one text per household. But "with the same message" — if multiple failed messages per household, which one? R12 lists 10 failed ids and 10 households, so likely one-to-one. Safest: dedupe per household, one resend per failed message but since 10 ids = 10 households, it's the same. I'll plan: iterate sent_messages(), for each with delivery_status()[id] == 'failed', re-queue via queue_sms with original template_id and params, deduplicating per household (skip if household already resent).
